title: Jude Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jude chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jude Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jude Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Jude 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: This is found in Jude 1:1, where Jude introduces himself as the servant of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Who is the brother of Jude mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Jude refers to himself as the brother of James in Jude 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is Jude writing in this chapter?
options: Them that are sanctified by God the Father
questions.correctAnswer: Them that are sanctified by God the Father
questions.explanation: Jude addresses the letter to those sanctified by God the Father in Jude 1:1.

questions.question: What does Jude wish for his readers in Jude 1:2?
questions.explanation: In Jude 1:2, Jude expresses a desire for mercy, peace, and love to be multiplied to his readers.

questions.question: What are believers urged to do in Jude 1:3?
questions.explanation: Jude encourages believers to earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints in Jude 1:3.

questions.question: What has happened to certain men mentioned in Jude 1:4?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:4 states that certain men have crept in unawares, indicating they infiltrated the community without recognition.

questions.question: What example does Jude give in Jude 1:5?
options: The people out of the land of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The people out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Jude 1:5 mentions how the Lord saved the people out of Egypt but later destroyed those who did not believe.

questions.question: What happened to the angels that left their first estate, according to Jude 1:6?
options: They were reserved in everlasting chains
questions.correctAnswer: They were reserved in everlasting chains
questions.explanation: Jude 1:6 explains that those angels who did not keep their estate are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness.

questions.question: What cities does Jude compare to the ungodly in Jude 1:7?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:7 specifically mentions Sodom and Gomorrha as examples of those giving themselves over to fornication.

questions.question: What do the filthy dreamers in Jude 1:8 do?
questions.explanation: In Jude 1:8, it is stated that these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.

questions.question: Who contended with the devil over the body of Moses according to Jude 1:9?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:9 mentions Michael the archangel contending with the devil about the body of Moses.

questions.question: Did Michael bring a railing accusation against the devil in Jude 1:9?
questions.explanation: According to Jude 1:9, Michael the archangel did not bring a railing accusation but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee.'

questions.question: Was Jude's purpose in writing to exhort the readers?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:3 states that it was needful for him to write and exhort them, indicating his purpose was to encourage them.

questions.question: Jude wrote to the people to encourage them to abandon their faith.
questions.explanation: This is false because Jude urges the believers to earnestly contend for the faith, not abandon it, as seen in Jude 1:3.

questions.question: The archangel Michael accused the devil of wrongdoing.
questions.explanation: This is false; Jude 1:9 states that Michael did not bring a railing accusation but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee.'

medium.title: Jude Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jude Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do those who speak evil corrupt themselves like, according to Jude 1:10?
questions.explanation: The answer is 'Brute beasts' because Jude 1:10 states that they speak evil of things they do not know, and what they know naturally, as brute beasts, they corrupt themselves.

questions.question: What does Jude 1:11 warn will happen to those who follow the way of Cain?
questions.explanation: The answer is 'They will perish' as Jude 1:11 declares woe to them for going the way of Cain and ultimately perishing.

questions.question: According to Jude 1:12, what are these ungodly individuals compared to?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:12 describes them as 'clouds they are without water,' indicating their emptiness and lack of substance.

questions.question: What do Jude 1:14-15 say the Lord will do upon His coming?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:15 states that the Lord comes to 'execute judgment upon all,' highlighting the seriousness of His return.

questions.question: What are the ungodly referred to in Jude 1:16?
questions.explanation: In Jude 1:16, they are described as 'murmurers, complainers,' indicating their negative behavior and attitude.

questions.question: What does Jude 1:17 remind believers to remember?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:17 encourages believers to remember the words spoken by the apostles of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: According to Jude 1:18, who will there be in the last time?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:18 specifically mentions that there will be 'mockers in the last time' who follow their own ungodly lusts.

questions.question: What imagery does Jude 1:13 use to describe the ungodly?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:13 refers to them as 'wandering stars,' indicating instability and impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Jude 1:12 say about the trees without fruit?
questions.explanation: According to Jude 1:12, these trees are described as 'without fruit, twice dead,' emphasizing their complete failure.

questions.question: What does Jude 1:5 remind believers about the people saved from Egypt?
options: They were later destroyed for unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: They were later destroyed for unbelief
questions.explanation: Jude 1:5 recalls how the Lord saved them but later destroyed those who did not believe, serving as a warning.

questions.question: According to Jude 1:10, what do these individuals speak evil of?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:10 states they speak evil of 'those things which they know not,' highlighting their ignorance.

questions.question: What behavior does Jude 1:8 attribute to the filthy dreamers?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:8 describes these individuals as 'filthy dreamers' who defile the flesh, showing their moral corruption.

questions.question: The statement 'the Lord rebuke thee' was said by whom according to Jude 1:9?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:9 states that Michael the archangel said, 'The Lord rebuke thee,' demonstrating his reliance on God's authority.

questions.question: The ungodly are said to be admired for their advantage according to Jude 1:16.
questions.explanation: Jude 1:16 indicates that they have 'great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage.'

questions.question: The angels that sinned are said to have been forgiven according to Jude 1:6.
questions.explanation: Jude 1:6 states they are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness, indicating they were not forgiven.

hard.title: Jude Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jude Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Jude 1:19, how are those who separate themselves described?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:19 states, 'These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.' This describes their nature as carnal and lacking the Spirit.

questions.question: What does Jude urge believers to do in Jude 1:20?
options: Building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: Building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Jude 1:20 exhorts believers to 'build up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost,' emphasizing spiritual growth and prayer.

questions.question: In Jude 1:21, what are believers instructed to keep themselves in?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:21 says, 'Keep yourselves in the love of God,' which is a direct instruction to remain in God's love.

questions.question: According to Jude 1:22, what attitude should believers have towards some of the individuals mentioned?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:22 instructs to have 'compassion, making a difference,' showing a merciful approach to some individuals.

questions.question: What does Jude 1:23 say about those who are saved with fear?
options: Pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh
Welcoming them with open arms regardless of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh
questions.explanation: Jude 1:23 describes saving others 'with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh,' emphasizing careful rescue and purity.

questions.question: In Jude 1:24, what is God able to do for believers?
options: Keep you from falling and present you faultless before his glory
questions.correctAnswer: Keep you from falling and present you faultless before his glory
questions.explanation: Jude 1:24 states God is 'able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,' highlighting divine protection and presentation.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'praying' (προσεύχομαι) in Jude 1:20 mean?
options: To offer petitions or supplications to God
To praise loudly in a congregation
questions.correctAnswer: To offer petitions or supplications to God
questions.explanation: The Greek verb 'προσεύχομαι' used in Jude 1:20 means 'to offer petitions or supplications to God,' emphasizing active prayer.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Jude 1:24-25?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:24-25 is a doxology, a liturgical expression of praise to God, giving glory, majesty, dominion, and power.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with Jude 1:6 about angels kept in everlasting chains?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:6 references angels kept in chains, connecting with Genesis 6:1-4 where 'sons of God' (interpreted as angels) left their habitation, a background for Jude's statement.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the warning about mockers in Jude 1:18?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:3 also warns of mockers in the last days who walk after their own lusts, echoing the theme of Jude 1:18.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Jude 1:19, describing those who separate themselves?
options: Jude 1:18, mentioning mockers in the last time
Jude 1:20, urging prayer in the Holy Ghost
Jude 1:21, about keeping in God's love
questions.correctAnswer: Jude 1:18, mentioning mockers in the last time
questions.explanation: Jude 1:18 directly precedes 1:19 and describes mockers in the last time, setting the stage for the description in verse 19.

questions.question: How does Jude 1:23 exemplify typology in its mention of 'pulling them out of the fire'?
options: It typifies salvation as rescue from judgment, foreshadowing final redemption
It typifies fiery trials as purification only
It refers solely to physical rescue from danger
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies salvation as rescue from judgment, foreshadowing final redemption
questions.explanation: The phrase 'pulling them out of the fire' in Jude 1:23 typifies salvation as rescue from judgment, a common biblical typology foreshadowing final redemption.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'garment spotted by the flesh' in Jude 1:23 from a cultural perspective?
options: It symbolizes moral impurity and defilement, reflecting Jewish purity laws
It literally refers to clothing stained with dirt
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes moral impurity and defilement, reflecting Jewish purity laws
questions.explanation: The 'garment spotted by the flesh' in Jude 1:23 symbolizes moral impurity, reflecting Jewish cultural emphasis on purity and holiness in daily life.

questions.question: True or False: Jude 1:25 ascribes both dominion and power to God our Savior.
questions.explanation: Jude 1:25 states, 'be glory and majesty, dominion and power,' attributing these to God our Savior.

questions.question: True or False: Jude 1:19 praises those who separate themselves as spiritually mature.
questions.explanation: Jude 1:19 describes those who separate themselves as 'sensual, having not the Spirit,' which is a negative description, not praise.

theological.title: Jude Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jude Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jude 1:3 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation is a common gift once delivered to the saints
Salvation is earned by human effort and works
Salvation is only for the elect and not for all saints
Salvation can be lost and regained repeatedly
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is a common gift once delivered to the saints
questions.explanation: Jude 1:3 emphasizes 'the common salvation' and the need to contend earnestly for 'the faith which was once delivered unto the saints,' indicating salvation is a shared gift delivered once.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jude 1:4 teach regarding human sin and divine judgment?
options: Certain ungodly men pervert God's grace and deny Jesus Christ, leading to condemnation
All men are saved regardless of their actions
Sin has no impact on salvation once grace is given
God's grace encourages licentiousness without accountability
questions.correctAnswer: Certain ungodly men pervert God's grace and deny Jesus Christ, leading to condemnation
questions.explanation: Jude 1:4 warns against ungodly men who turn God's grace into lasciviousness and deny Jesus Christ, showing the doctrine of judgment for persistent sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jude 1:6 teach about angelic beings and eschatological judgment?
options: Angels who abandoned their proper domain are reserved in eternal chains until judgment
All angels are free and have no future judgment
Angels can repent and be restored to their first estate
Angels are not subject to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Angels who abandoned their proper domain are reserved in eternal chains until judgment
questions.explanation: Jude 1:6 clearly states that angels who did not keep their first estate are kept in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jude 1:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:5 recalls how the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after being saved out of Egypt, demonstrating God's attribute of justice in punishing unbelief.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jude 1:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:24 speaks of God’s ability to keep believers from falling and present them faultless, demonstrating His sovereign power to preserve the faithful.

questions.question: How does Jude 1:7 contribute to the biblical narrative arc of divine judgment on sin?
options: It recalls the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as a warning of eternal fire for sexual immorality
It shows that all cities are equally judged regardless of sin
It emphasizes repentance and restoration of sinful cities
It teaches that God overlooks sins of fornication
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as a warning of eternal fire for sexual immorality
questions.explanation: Jude 1:7 uses Sodom and Gomorrah as examples of divine judgment for fornication and unnatural lust, fitting the biblical theme of God’s judgment on sin.

questions.question: In what way does Jude 1:14-15 connect to Old Testament prophecy and eschatological fulfillment?
options: It cites Enoch’s prophecy about the Lord coming with His saints to execute judgment, linking to final day judgment themes
It denies any prophetic tradition preceding the New Testament
It teaches that Enoch foretold the destruction of Israel only
It claims no judgment will come upon the ungodly
questions.correctAnswer: It cites Enoch’s prophecy about the Lord coming with His saints to execute judgment, linking to final day judgment themes
questions.explanation: Jude 1:14-15 refers to Enoch’s prophecy of the Lord coming with ten thousands of saints to judge the ungodly, connecting the epistle to Jewish apocalyptic tradition and eschatology.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Jude 1:3 and Jude 1:21 teach about sanctification and perseverance?
options: Believers are called to contend earnestly for the faith and keep themselves in God's love, looking for mercy
Sanctification is automatic and requires no vigilance
Faith can be lost but love is permanent without effort
Perseverance depends solely on human effort without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to contend earnestly for the faith and keep themselves in God's love, looking for mercy
questions.explanation: Jude 1:3 exhorts believers to earnestly contend for the faith, and Jude 1:21 commands to keep in the love of God while looking for mercy, together teaching active perseverance in sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Jude 1:4 and Jude 1:10 teach about false teachers and their knowledge?
options: False teachers pervert grace and speak evil of things they do not know, corrupting themselves
False teachers have perfect knowledge and teach truth
False teachers are divinely inspired prophets
False teachers are harmless and not a threat to the church
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers pervert grace and speak evil of things they do not know, corrupting themselves
questions.explanation: Jude 1:4 warns of men turning grace into lasciviousness and denying Christ, and Jude 1:10 says they speak evil of things they do not know, corrupting themselves, revealing their dangerous ignorance and sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Jude 1:12 and Jude 1:13 teach about the nature and judgment of false teachers?
options: False teachers are described as unfruitful spots and wandering stars destined for eternal darkness
False teachers are fruitful and rewarded by God
False teachers are temporary and will be restored
False teachers are merely misguided but not condemned
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers are described as unfruitful spots and wandering stars destined for eternal darkness
questions.explanation: Jude 1:12 calls them spots without fear feeding themselves, and Jude 1:13 calls them wandering stars reserved for blackness of darkness forever, indicating their corrupt nature and eternal condemnation.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jude 1:9 teaches that Michael the archangel has authority to judge Satan directly. What does Jude 1:9 actually teach?
options: Michael did not bring a railing accusation but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee,' showing judgment belongs to God alone
Michael exercised his own authority to condemn Satan
Michael and Satan negotiated a truce
Michael ignored Satan and took no part in the dispute
questions.correctAnswer: Michael did not bring a railing accusation but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee,' showing judgment belongs to God alone
questions.explanation: Jude 1:9 states Michael did not accuse Satan directly but invoked the Lord’s rebuke, highlighting divine prerogative in judgment, not angelic authority.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jude 1:8 teach about the character of false teachers?
options: False teachers are defilers of the flesh, despise authority, and slander dignitaries
False teachers are humble and respect authority
False teachers promote holiness and purity
False teachers avoid controversy and remain silent
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers are defilers of the flesh, despise authority, and slander dignitaries
questions.explanation: Jude 1:8 describes false teachers as 'filthy dreamers' who defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities, revealing their corrupt character.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in Jude 1:25 ascribed to God?
questions.explanation: Jude 1:25 calls God the 'only wise God our Saviour,' emphasizing His divine attribute of wisdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jude 1:16 and Jude 1:19 teach about the behavior and spiritual condition of false teachers?
options: They are murmurers, walking according to lusts, and lack the Spirit
They are meek and submissive to church authority
They are united and doctrinally sound
questions.correctAnswer: They are murmurers, walking according to lusts, and lack the Spirit
questions.explanation: Jude 1:16 describes them as murmurers and complainers following lusts, and 1:19 says they are sensual and have not the Spirit, showing their corrupt nature and spiritual emptiness.

questions.question: How does Jude 1:22-23 illustrate the church's pastoral responsibility toward sinners?
options: Showing compassion with discernment and saving some with fear, pulling them out of the fire
Accepting all sinners without call to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Showing compassion with discernment and saving some with fear, pulling them out of the fire
questions.explanation: Jude 1:22-23 teaches believers to have compassion, making distinctions among sinners, and to save others with fear, emphasizing careful pastoral care.
